Article Title: 'Unforgivable': MP minister Vishvas Sarang slams Kharge over remark on PM Modi
Article Text:
In a recent event marking Dr. Krishna Singh's birth anniversary in Patna, Madhya Pradesh minister Vishvas Sarang took aim at Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge for his disparaging remarks about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's late parents. (Pic Credit: ANI)

Controversy erupts at Patna event

Madhya Pradesh minister Vishvas Sarang on Monday criticised Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his remarks referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s late parents, describing the language as “unforgivable” and accusing the Congress of disregarding Indian values and traditions.According to the news agency ANI, Sarang alleged that Kharge had crossed all limits and claimed that the remarks reflected the Congress’s political frustration.“The Congress is constantly acting against our values and traditions. The language used about Narendra Modi ji’s late mother and father is unforgivable. Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi and other Congress leaders have also made objectionable remarks about the Prime Minister’s late mother and insulted her previously. Kharge ji crossed all limits yesterday,” Sarang said.He further questioned the appropriateness of such remarks from an experienced political leader, arguing that Indian cultural traditions call for respect when referring to the deceased.“Such behaviour is not expected from a person aged 70, 75 or 80. He used those words not once, but three times. Kharge ji, you are breaking traditions. This is a highly condemnable act.Don’t you understand the traditions of India? In our culture, such language is not used for a deceased person,” the minister said.Sarang also maintained that political disagreements with the Prime Minister should not justify the use of such language. He accused the Congress of allowing political frustration to influence its public statements.“You may have political differences with Narendra Modi ji, but how far will you take politics? This reflects the Congress’s frustration. Kharge ji has torn apart our traditions. This is disgusting, and I feel disgusted by it,” he added.The Madhya Pradesh minister also expressed displeasure over the Congress’s alleged failure to respond to the controversy within 24 hours, calling the silence unfortunate.“Even after 24 hours, there has been no response from the Congress. This is very unfortunate,” Sarang said.The controversy began on Sunday when Kharge addressed an event in Patna marking the 139th birth anniversary of Dr Krishna Singh, Bihar’s first Chief Minister.During the programme, an attendee interrupted the Congress president, saying that Prime Minister Modi would not go anywhere. In response, Kharge reportedly said from the stage, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” (Even Modi’s father will have to go).The remark drew sharp criticism from senior BJP leaders and union ministers, who accused the Congress of lowering the standards of political discourse and attributed the statement to electoral frustration.
Article Summary: Madhya Pradesh minister Vishvas Sarang criticised Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his remarks referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's late parents. Sarang alleged that Kharge had crossed all limits and claimed that the remarks reflected the Congress’s political frustration. The controversy began on Sunday when Kharge addressed an event in Patna marking the 139th birth anniversary of Dr Krishna Singh.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday congratulated Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his re-election, saying India and Brazil would work together to strengthen cooperation and advance the shared priorities of the Global South.In a post on X, Modi described Lula as his "dear friend" and said he looked forward to deepening and expanding the India-Brazil Strategic Partnership."Heartiest congratulations to my dear friend, President Lula, on his remarkable re-election victory. Article Title: BJP calls protest over Kharge’s ‘baap’ remark
Article Text:

Not the first time Cong has abused Modi or his family, says Shah

PATNA/NEW DELHI: Congress party president Mallikarjun Kharge ’s remark about PM Narendra Modi ’s father raised a furore in BJP on Sunday, with the party announcing a nationwide protest on Monday against Kharge’s “indecent and offensive” remarks.Addressing a gathering at Bapu Sabhagar in Patna, Kharge was interrupted by a young member of the audience who shouted “Modi nahin jayega (Modi will not go)”. The Congress chief shot back, saying, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega (Modi’s father, too, will have to go)”.The youth was removed from the venue by the organisers of the function marking the 139th birth anniversary of Bihar’s first chief minister Shri Krishna Sinha.Union home minister Amit Shah targeted Congress for its frequent personal attacks on Modi and blamed it on simmering frustration within the party over its continuous poll losses over the last 12 years."Kharge has broken all norms of decency by commenting on Modi’s father,” Shah said, adding Congress was frequently crossing the limits of decency under Rahul Gandhi . “This is not the first time Congress has abused Modi or his family,” he said, recalling barbs like “maut ka saudagar” for him and abusive reference to his mother.BJP announced the protests against Congress after an organisational meeting, which was presided over by party chief Nitin Nabin and Shah. Nabin said a certain decorum was expected of the political opposition but it had now become a trend for Rahul and the entire opposition to drag dead family members in their speeches. BJP MP Dharmendra Pradhan said, “Having forgotten the bounds of propriety in political opposition, Congress is now resorting solely to personal insults.Stepping up his attack on BJP over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Kharge described the ongoing protests against the exercise as the “second war for independence”.“If people have no voting rights, the country will be enslaved. It (the protests) is the second war for independence. We will have to fight for our vote, voting rights, for democracy and to save the Constitution,” Kharge said, demanding the rollback of SIR and the use of ballot papers in elections. He alleged “vote chori” in Haryana, Maharashtra, Bihar and West Bengal, and demanded govts formed through stolen votes be removed.Kharge targeted BJP ally and JD(U) national president Nitish Kumar, saying he had roots in the socialist ideology of Ram Manohar Lohia and Jayaprakash Narayan but ended up in the “lap of BJP and RSS”. Rahul Gandhi, he said, “is alive, is fighting, and also forging ahead by taking all along with him”.
Article Summary: Congress party president Mallikarjun Kharge’s remark about PM Narendra Modi ’s father raised a furore in BJP on Sunday. The party announced a nationwide protest on Monday against Kharge's “indecent and offensive” remarks.

Article Title: Mallikarjun Kharge’s 'baap' remark on PM Modi sparks row, BJP hits back
Article Text:
Targeting PM Modi further, Kharge called the prime minister a “habitual liar”

BJP hits back

Congress accuses BJP of 'disrespecting' Kharge again

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge triggered a controversy on Sunday with his remark, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” (Modi’s father will also be defeated), at a programme in Patna.In a video shared by ANI, a person can be heard shouting, “Modi nahi jayega” (Modi will not be defeated), prompting a response from Kharge.“Modi ka baap bhi jayega … baap bhi jayega,” the Congress president retorted, as party workers escorted the person out of the hall.Targeting PM Modi further, Kharge called the prime minister a “habitual liar”.“PM Modi has a habit of telling lies. He had promised to bring back black money within his first 100 days. I want to ask, where is that money?” Kharge asked.The BJP hit back, with Union home minister Amit Shah accusing Kharge of crossing all limits. Shah attributed the Congress’s “frustration” to its repeated electoral defeats since 2014."This is not the first time that the Congress party has used abusive language against Modior his family. At times, they have used derogatory remarks about his revered mother; at other times, they have labelled him a 'maut ka saudagar' (merchant of death); and on other occasions, they have mocked his humble background by calling him a 'chaiwala' (tea seller). Under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi, the Congress party is crossing the boundaries of indecency with each passing day," Shah wrote in Hindi on X, referring to remarks by Congress leaders against the prime minister."Having faced consecutive electoral defeats over the past 12 years, the Congress party has become so mired in frustration and despair that it is now left with neither a coherent policy nor any substantive issues—only a politics of abuse. Having already lost public support, the Congress is now losing its footing even among its own party workers," he added.The home minister further stated that the public would give the Congress a “befitting reply”, as it had in the past whenever party leaders used alleged indecent language against PM Modi or his family.BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari attributed Kharge’s remarks to the Congress’s frustration over what he predicted would be a poor turnout at the party’s upcoming rally in Delhi.“Frustration of Congress is out in the open! Knowing its 1st November rally is about to be a flop show, knowing Rahul Gandhi's anarchy is being called out, knowing it is not getting support of People of India; Congress frustration is out in the open! Congress statement proves People of India are with PM Modi,” Bhandari posted on X.The Congress and its allies are scheduled to hold a rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1 to protest alleged “vote chori” by the Election Commission in favour of the ruling BJP.Meanwhile, the Congress alleged that the person who shouted "Modi nahi jayega" was a BJP worker and accused the party of "disrespecting" Kharge again after the alleged purification incident in Uttarakhand."Previously, they (BJP) engaged in a despicable act, so-called purification ritual in Uttarakhand, solely because he (Kharge) is a Dalit. Today, in Bihar, while Kharge ji was delivering a speech, a BJP worker rudely said that Modi will not go anywhere; even if your own father were to come," Congress MP Pawan Khera told ANI.Khera claimed that the Congress chief's "baap" reference was for the RSS, the BJP's ideological mentor, and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat."In response, Kharge ji retorted that Modi will indeed go and so will his father referring to his ideological mentor: the Sangh, and Mohan Bhagwat. This repeated disrespect toward our national president is happening at the direct behest of Modi and Shah. The nation will not forgive this. The nation is watching," he added.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge triggered a controversy on Sunday with his remark, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega” (Modi’s father will also be defeated), at a programme in Patna. Targeting PM Modi further, Kharge called the prime minister a “habitual liar’ Union home minister Amit Shah accused Kharge of crossing all limits.

Article Title: 'Pakistan has no right': Congress distances itself from ally Farooq Abdullah's Kashmiri remark
Article Text:
J&K Congress distances itself from Farooq Abdullah's Pakistan remarks; Kashmiri Pandit groups seek FIR

What Farooq Abdullah said

NEW DELHI: The Jammu and Kashmir Congress has distanced itself from National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah’s remarks that Pakistan was helping Kashmiris by keeping the Kashmir issue alive at international fora.“The Jammu and Kashmir Pradesh Congress Committee has distanced itself from the statement of NC president Farooq Abdullah and asserted that Pakistan has no right to talk about or interfere in our internal affairs as J&K is an integral part of India,” J&K Congress chief spokesperson Ravinder Sharma said in a post on X.However, speaking to reporters, Sharma said Abdullah’s remarks appeared to reflect frustration over the Centre’s failure to fulfil its promise to restore statehood to Jammu and Kashmir.“Pakistan has consistently waged a proxy war against India and caused the deaths of innocent people in J&K by sponsoring terrorism. Pakistan’s role in promoting terrorism must be condemned, and strict action should continue against it,” Sharma said, reiterating that the Congress was firmly opposed to any interference by Pakistan in India’s internal affairs.Sharma said Abdullah should clarify the intent behind his remarks, adding that opposition to Pakistan-sponsored terrorism and the demand for restoration of statehood were separate but equally important issues.He also suggested that Abdullah’s comments were directed at what he described as discrimination against minorities across the country and the policies pursued by BJP governments in various states.“The remarks reflected resentment against a pattern of oppression and discrimination,” the Congress leader said.Sharma further said Jammu and Kashmir continued to face resentment over the delay in restoring statehood, despite repeated assurances by the Centre before the Supreme Court, Parliament and the public.Meanwhile, some Kashmiri Pandit groups have filed a police complaint seeking an FIR against the former chief minister over his comments.His remarks drew criticism from some Kashmiri Pandit groups, which lodged a police complaint seeking the registration of an FIR against the former chief minister.Meanwhile, Kashmiri Pandit groups Panun Kashmir and the Jammu State People's Movement (JSPM) have lodged a police complaint at the Channi police station in Jammu, seeking the registration of an FIR against Abdullah over his remarks.The complaint, submitted by Panun Kashmir chairman Tito Ganju and JSPM chairman Col Ajay Raina (retd), sought an investigation into statements attributed to Abdullah concerning the constitutional status of Jammu and Kashmir and alleged religious polarisation.It cited his reported remarks questioning the prospects of justice from the Union government and warning that the people of J&K risked losing their identity if they failed to confront the prevailing political circumstances.The complainants also referred to remarks attributed to Abdullah about the demolition of mosques, homes and shops, as well as his assertion that Hindus and Muslims were being pitted against each other. They urged the police to examine the statements in their entirety, taking into account their context, the audience addressed and their potential implications.The complaint sought an FIR under Sections 152, 196 and 197 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with any other provisions that may apply based on the investigation.The provisions cited concern acts endangering India's sovereignty, unity and integrity, promoting enmity between groups, and certain imputations or assertions prejudicial to national integration, a Panun Kashmir spokesperson said.BJP leader Jahanzaib Sirwal also criticised Abdullah, accusing him of double standards for invoking Pakistan to question India's intentions while overlooking the suffering of people across the Line of Control.“It was deeply unfortunate that a leader who has dominated J&K’s political landscape for decades continues to rely on the Pakistan narrative rather than account for the consequences of his own politics.“Farooq Sahib has spent decades building a political narrative around Pakistan, but has he ever honestly answered what this politics has delivered to the people of J&K?“His party does not have to seek votes in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir, but that cannot be an excuse to remain silent on the atrocities and sufferings of the people living there. Human rights cannot be selective, and political morality cannot change with electoral convenience,” Sirwal said.He added that the NC leadership must stop treating Pakistan as a convenient political instrument to invoke whenever it suited its narrative.Addressing a party event in Baramulla on Saturday, Abdullah questioned whether people in Jammu and Kashmir could expect justice from the Centre.“What hope will you (people of J&K) have from them (Delhi)? Will you expect that they will do justice for you?" he said.Urging Kashmiris to remain courageous in confronting Delhi, Abdullah warned that their identity could disappear if they failed to do so.“If not, you will be erased. Even our trace and identity will disappear. They are silent today because there is noise in the world, and our neighbour is constantly behind this. Everywhere they say, 'the decision regarding Kashmir has not been made'. That is what is saving us. Otherwise, their intentions are not good,” he said.
Article Summary: J&K Congress distances itself from Farooq Abdullah's Pakistan remarks. Kashmiri Pandit groups seek FIR against the former chief minister. Abdullah questioned whether people in Jammu and Kashmir could expect justice from the Centre. He said Pakistan was helping Kashmiris by keeping the Kashmir issue alive.

Article Title: 'Some still allow political calculations': Jaishankar's veiled swipe days after Rubio backs Pak ties
Article Text:
Jaishankar said some countries continued to allow political calculations to take precedence despite lessons of history.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said that the use of terrorism as an “instrument of statecraft” was unacceptable and could never be justified, warning that the threat persisted because some countries did not demonstrate “zero tolerance”.Speaking at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan on the occasion of UN Day, Jaishankar said some countries continued to allow political considerations to take precedence despite the lessons of history.“Terrorism is another deadly threat to peace. Its usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable. It can never be justified. It can never be rationalised. Yet, it continues because not all states really display zero tolerance,” he said.“Despite history holding so many lessons, some still allow political calculations to take precedence. The world must therefore develop sharper awareness about this common threat, and it must come together with stronger resolve and counter-terrorism in all its forms and manifestations,” he added. Jaishankar did not name any country in his remarks.Earlier this week, US secretary of state Marco Rubio defended Washington’s engagement with Pakistan saying the US needed to maintain relations with countries with which it had disagreements.Speaking to Network18, Rubio said Pakistan’s possession of nuclear weapons and its geographical position made engagement necessary.He also argued that maintaining ties could give Washington greater influence over Islamabad’s decisions, including on terrorism.“In the case of Pakistan, it’s a country that we have to have a relationship with, a country that possesses nuclear weapons. It’s a country that from a geographic standpoint, we need to be able to interact with them in much the same way as govt of India has to have and has a relationship and meets with leaders from Iran,” Rubio said.“... It could be a positive thing because if... we can speak to them, it perhaps puts us in a position to help discourage the kinds of things India is worried about,” he added.Rubio also urged businesses to view India-US ties as a strategic partnership spanning technology, trade and security. He said the two countries were “perfectly aligned” on issues shaping the 21st century, while acknowledging that differences would persist.Jaishankar also stressed the importance of peace amid ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and West Asia, warning that wars in one part of the world can have far-reaching consequences for global security, economies and societies."We cannot remain helpless spectators. India expresses global sentiment when we urge that dialogue and diplomacy are the only solution," the external affairs minister said.Emphasising the interconnected nature of global peace, he said, "Let us consider the indivisibility of peace. Now, war anywhere threatens peace everywhere."Jaishankar said India was making efforts towards peacebuilding and remained open to working with other partners to advance these efforts.The minister also highlighted the link between peace, economic progress and shared prosperity, warning that unequal development in an interconnected world could fuel further instability."Progress and prosperity are the flip side of conflict and violence, and they too are equally indivisible. The world cannot advance half prosperous and half denied in an era of intricate supply chains, of globalised markets, and of common resources. This is simply a prescription for continuous instability," he said.His remarks came a day after India condemned a deadly attack on a church in Karak, Jordan, on October 23, which killed seven people and injured 34 others.In a statement, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) described the attack as “heinous” and “cowardly”, extended condolences to the bereaved families and wished those injured a speedy recovery.Jaishankar also called for reforms in the United Nations, saying the organisation's shortcomings and limitations needed to be acknowledged and addressed. He said the case for reformed multilateralism was becoming increasingly compelling."Large parts of the world cannot be left out from decision-making. The UN must show leadership, not be a spectator to global crises," he said.Calling for collective efforts to strengthen the international body, he added, "On this occasion, even as we recognise the need for such long-awaited changes, let us renew our commitment to work together. We are common, we are shared, we are united."
Article Summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said use of terrorism as an “instrument of statecraft’ was unacceptable and could never be justified. He said some countries continued to allow political considerations to take precedence despite the lessons of history. JaISHankar did not name any country in his remarks.

Article Title: Centre rushes 250 RAF personnel to Arunachal after violent protests over hydropower project

NEW DELHI: The Centre has sent two companies of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to Arunachal Pradesh following violence in Pasighat during protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, officials said on Sunday.The ministry of home affairs (MHA) directed on Saturday that the two companies, comprising around 250 personnel, be airlifted from Navi Mumbai aboard an Indian Air Force transport aircraft. The units are expected to reach Pasighat and be deployed by Sunday, officials told news agency PTI.The RAF is a specialised anti-riot unit of the CRPF whose personnel wear blue uniforms.Several CRPF units are already deployed in the violence-hit areas. Arunachal Pradesh also has a permanent deployment of around two to three CRPF battalions.Officials said CRPF personnel had effectively handled the protests since Friday and prevented the violence from escalating. Several police and central forces personnel were injured during the clashes, they added.On Friday night, a mob torched an NHPC office and a police station and vandalised the residences of three political leaders, including the state BJP president, in East Siang district, according to Arunachal Pradesh Police officials.Arunachal chief minister Pema Khandu said the right to peaceful protest was an essential part of democracy, but stressed that demonstrations must remain within the bounds of the law and should not lead to property damage or disruption of public order.Describing the incidents in Pasighat as regrettable, Khandu appealed to all sections of society to maintain peace.According to a statement issued by the chief minister's Office (CMO), a 12-hour bandh in Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts over the proposed power project remained largely peaceful on Friday. However, violence broke out in Pasighat after the bandh ended and continued until 3.30 am on Saturday.Protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP) turned violent in Pasighat, East Siang district, on Friday night, with "Gen Z" protesters allegedly setting fire to the NHPC office and a police station and vandalising and looting the residences of two MLAs and the state BJP president, police said.The violence continued in waves for nearly nine hours into Saturday morning, leaving "over 40 police personnel injured in stone-pelting", police said. A protester was hit in the leg by a tear gas shell and admitted to hospital.Following the violence, the East Siang district administration imposed restrictions on public gatherings and processions in Pasighat, Mebo and Ruksin, citing fears of vandalism, arson and a possible breach of law and order amid protests and bandh-related activities.India’s proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, planned across three districts of Arunachal, is being pitched as a strategic counter to China’s mega dam upstream. But the plan has faced resistance from indigenous tribes, who fear the reservoir could submerge villages and sever their deep-rooted ties with the river.Known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet, the Siang enters Arunachal Pradesh near Gelling and flows for 294km before meeting the Dibang and Lohit rivers at Sadiya in Assam to form the Brahmaputra.
Article Summary: The Centre has sent two companies of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) to Arunachal Pradesh. The RAF is a specialised anti- riot unit of the CRPF whose personnel wear blue uniforms. Several police and central forces personnel were injured during the clashes.

NEW DELHI: Keralam BJP president and former Union minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar on Sunday said chief minister VD Satheesan should refrain from encouraging “Jinnah worship”, accusing him of indulging in “selective secularism. "His remarks came in response to a social media post by Satheesan after a YouTuber was booked for allegedly making communal remarks in a video. The vlogger claimed that a cafe in Fort Kochi displayed a statue of Pakistan’s founder, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, and served beef despite being named after the holy city of Kashi (Varanasi) in Uttar Pradesh.The video, shared on Instagram, triggered widespread criticism, with Satheesan and leader of opposition and former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan condemning the alleged communal remarks. Fort Kochi police registered a case against Amrit Singh Darren, a YouTuber from a northern Indian state, under relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) over the video."Do not encourage anti-India, anti-Hindu insults/discourse/actions/sentiment like Jinnah worship. In that, you will have our support. But selective secularism and selective talk of communal harmony will make you like every other fake politician before you. And we will resist it. Fully. Everytime," Chandrashekhar wrote in the post.While agreeing with the sentiment expressed by Satheesan, Chandrashekhar questioned the presence of Jinnah’s statue, the alleged justification of violence by proscribed terrorist organisations such as Hamas, and the Congress and CPI(M)’s political alliances with Jamaat-e-Islami, which he accused of being “anti-secular” and “anti-constitutional."In his post, Chandrashekhar asserted that "Keralam belongs to all Malayalees," who alone had the right to decide the state’s present and future, including its food, culture and celebrations.Citing Articles 19 and 19(2) of the Constitution, the former Union minister maintained that the right to freedom of speech and expression, along with the restrictions governing it, applied equally to all Indians.He called on the chief minister to show equal sensitivity and respect towards Hindus, Christians and Muslims, while cautioning against what he described as anti-India and anti-Hindu insults and discourse.
Article Summary: Keralam BJP president and former Union minister Rajeev Chandrashekhar said chief minister VD Satheesan should refrain from encouraging "Jinnah worship" His remarks came in response to a social media post bySatheesan after a YouTuber was booked for allegedly making communal remarks in a video.

The Border Security Force (BSF) has apprehended four Pakistani fishermen who allegedly entered Indian waters for crab-catching activities and seized a fishing boat near the India-Pakistan border in Gujarat’s Kutch district.According to news agency PTI, the fishermen were apprehended from the Sir Creek area on Sunday following specific intelligence inputs, an official said. Article Title: ‘Prioritise welfare over military directives’: India raps Pak on minority rights at UN

NEW DELHI: India tore into Pakistan at the United Nations for exploiting the international forum to spread propaganda while failing to protect its own citizens. New Delhi reiterated that Jammu and Kashmir remains an integral and inalienable part of India and demanded that Pakistan vacate all territories under its illegal occupation.Speaking at an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Minority Issues at the UN General Assembly's Third Committee, India's First Secretary at the Permanent Mission to the UN, Raghoo Puri, called out Pakistan's conduct and said its representatives should focus on the welfare of their own people instead of taking directions from the military."Pakistan predictably misused the forum for propaganda. Jammu & Kashmir is an integral and inalienable part of India. Pakistan must vacate the territory under its illegal occupation," Puri said.He further said Pakistani representatives would do well to look inwards and address the concerns of their own citizens rather than act on military directives.Puri underlined that protecting minority rights was primarily the sovereign responsibility of individual states, guided by the principle of sovereign equality.He said India's civilisational tradition of diversity was reflected in its constitutional safeguards for religious and linguistic minorities.He also highlighted the substantial contributions made by minorities to India's national development, including at the highest levels of government and key institutions.The latest confrontation followed India's strong rebuke to Pakistan at the UN on October 23 over its treatment of religious minorities. New Delhi accused Islamabad of failing to protect vulnerable communities while attempting to lecture India on religious freedom, burial rights and minority protections.During an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Religion or Belief, India's First Secretary at the UN mission, Bhavika Mangalanandan, challenged the report's approach to religious discrimination during the Covid-19 pandemic and its advocacy concerning funeral rights for terrorists.Mangalanandan argued that the report appeared to place disproportionate emphasis on discriminatory practices and shortcomings in countries in the Global South while overlooking similar tragedies in developed nations.Separately, India also defended its approach to climate change at the UN General Assembly, stressing the importance of equity, climate justice and sustainable development.Deputy secretary Barkha Tamrakar delivered India's statement before the Third Committee on the report of the Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers, titled “An urgent and existential threat: the role of justice systems in addressing the climate crisis.”Tamrakar described climate change as a serious global challenge with consequences for development, livelihoods and human rights. She said India's response was guided by equity, climate justice, sustainable development and the principle of Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC).She highlighted the Constitution, environmental legislation, the National Green Tribunal and an independent judiciary as key safeguards supporting environmental protection in India.Tamrakar also noted that the Supreme Court had recognised the fundamental rights to life and equality as essential protections against the adverse effects of climate change.On judicial independence, she pointed to transparent, institutionally supervised training programmes, including those conducted by the National Judicial Academy, as measures to strengthen impartiality and safeguard the independence of the judiciary.
Article Summary: New Delhi reiterates that Jammu and Kashmir remains an integral and inalienable part of India. India's First Secretary at the Permanent Mission to the UN, Raghoo Puri, called out Pakistan's conduct. Puri said Pakistani representatives should focus on the welfare of their own people instead of taking directions from the military.

Article Title: ‘Brazil is no one’s backyard’: Lula's jibe at US after winning fourth presidential term
Article Text:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Donald Trump

Lula calls for broader public participation

Cost of living, crime shape campaign

Trump administration looms over ties

NEW DELHI: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth presidential term after defeating conservative challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday’s runoff election, with the electoral authority confirming his victory and extending left-wing leadership in Latin America’s largest economy.Addressing supporters in São Paulo after his re-election, Lula said, “BRAZIL IS NO ONE'S BACKYARD,” in an apparent swipe at US influence in the region, after defeating Flávio Bolsonaro, who had advocated closer ties with the Trump administration. He also called for the regulation of digital platforms, claiming Brazil had defeated foreign intervention through them.“We need to regulate digital platforms,” Lula said, adding that his campaign had managed to counter foreign interference through digital platforms.With more than 78% of votes counted, Lula was leading with 51.21% against Bolsonaro’s 48.79%, according to Reuters’ live election coverage. Pollster Datafolha had projected Lula’s victory before the electoral authority officially confirmed the result.Meanwhile, Flávio Bolsonaro called for Brazil's election results to be 'annulled' after Lula da Silva.The victory marks a setback for US President Donald Trump’s allies in Latin America.Flávio Bolsonaro, a senator and son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, had campaigned on strengthening ties with Washington and securing better trade deals with the Trump administration.Lula, who previously governed Brazil from 2003 to 2010, had criticised US tariffs on Brazilian exports and Washington’s designation of drug-trafficking groups as foreign terrorist organisations.In his victory speech, Lula pledged to work with Brazil’s conservative-led Congress, despite political differences, and said he would govern for the entire country.“I will govern for 215 million Brazilians, we no longer have an electoral rival,” Lula said, seeking to strike a conciliatory note after a closely contested campaign that deepened political divisions.He also promised changes to the country’s governance and greater public involvement in policymaking.“We will change the way we run this country, we will make people participate more in decision-making process,” he said.Lula said his campaign had convinced voters that participating in the election was essential to protecting Brazil’s democratic institutions.“We managed to convince people that voting was extremely important to safeguard democracy in Brazil,” he said.The election pitted two sharply polarised political camps against each other, with the campaign dominated by disagreements over relations with the United States, crime, climate policy and social welfare.Lula’s victory gives Brazil and Mexico left-of-centre leadership in two of Latin America’s largest economies, while dealing a setback to conservative forces seeking closer alignment with Trump’s administration.Lula faced a challenging re-election battle amid voter concerns over the cost of living and crime. Bolsonaro made a tough-on-crime agenda central to his campaign and promised to reduce food prices, while Lula offered financial incentives to attract undecided voters.Both political camps were also dogged by corruption allegations involving allies and family members. Bolsonaro faced scrutiny over a sprawling scandal, while Lula had previously spent more than a year in prison following corruption convictions that were later annulled.The runoff was a rematch between two political forces that have divided Brazil in recent years. In the previous presidential election, Lula defeated Jair Bolsonaro by the narrowest margin since the country’s return to democracy in 1985.Flávio Bolsonaro had led Lula by more than 2.2 million votes in the first round earlier this month, setting the stage for a closely fought runoff.Lula’s supporters backed him for his record on poverty reduction and support for marginalised communities. Bolsonaro’s supporters, meanwhile, pointed to high prices and taxes and accused Lula’s political camp of corruption.US policy towards Brazil emerged as a major issue during the campaign, with Lula criticising Trump’s trade measures and approach to tackling organised crime.Flávio Bolsonaro emphasised his links with the White House and argued that Brazil needed better deals with the Trump administration, including in the rare-earth minerals sector. Brazil estimates that it holds deposits of up to 21 million tonnes of rare-earth resources, second only to China.Bolsonaro denied receiving assistance from the US government.Trump said on Sunday that he was following the Brazilian election but declined to endorse either candidate.Lula’s re-election is expected to keep disagreements over trade, US influence and regional diplomacy at the centre of relations between Brasília and Washington.
Article Summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins a fourth presidential term. Lula defeated conservative challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday’s runoff election. With more than 78% of votes counted, Lula was leading with 51.21 per cent.

Article Title: ‘I am here. With you’: Nobel laureate, Venezuela opposition leader Machado returns after nearly a year in exile
Article Text:
File photo: In this photo released by Vente Venezuela Press Office, Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado greets supporters at a church in Barquisimeto, Venezuela

Machado’s exile

Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday after nearly a year in exile. Her team confirmed her return, in a move likely to increase pressure on interim president Delcy Rodríguez as the country’s political future remains uncertain.“I am here. With you,” Machado wrote in Spanish on X, without disclosing how she had re-entered the country or providing details of her whereabouts.Her close ally, exiled opposition leader Edmundo González Urrutia, also confirmed her return in a social media post. “Venezuela! I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear María Corina, is on Venezuelan soil,” he wrote, adding that he would return soon.Machado was later seen at a church in Barquisimeto, the capital of Lara state, about 220 miles west of Caracas. Footage and photographs published by news organisations showed supporters greeting and embracing her during a religious ceremony at the Sanctuary of the Divine Shepherdess.Machado left Venezuela covertly in December 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway. Since then, she has made several attempts to return, but Venezuelan authorities blocked her entry, according to her party and her advisers. Her return comes amid continuing uncertainty over the country’s political transition following the removal of former president Nicolás Maduro by US forces in January.Machado’s opposition movement is widely believed to have won the 2024 presidential election, although Maduro was declared the winner and refused to hand over power. González, who stood in the election after Machado was barred from running, has been living in exile.Following Maduro’s ouster, Rodríguez, his former vice-president, assumed the role of interim president with the backing of US president Donald Trump’s administration. Washington has prioritised economic stabilisation and access to Venezuela’s oil, while Machado and her allies have pressed for a date for fresh presidential elections.The Guardian reported that the Trump administration had opposed Machado’s return, fearing it could complicate its relationship with Rodríguez. However, Trump told reporters on Sunday that he did not know about Machado’s return, adding that he hoped she was safe. “She’s a very nice woman,” he said, referring to the Nobel Peace Prize medal Machado had given him.US secretary of state Marco Rubio said the circumstances that enabled Machado’s return were the result of US support for reconciliation talks. In a post on X, Rubio said Washington expected the freedoms of all sectors of Venezuelan politics to be respected and urged political actors to support negotiations aimed at achieving free and fair elections.Machado’s homecoming comes as her party continues to demand an electoral timetable. Rodríguez’s interim administration has held rounds of negotiations with a section of the opposition and agreed to judicial reforms, but no date for a presidential election has been announced.Machado has repeatedly praised Trump for the operation that removed Maduro and presented him with her Nobel medal during a meeting in January. Her return now puts renewed focus on whether Venezuela’s political transition will lead to competitive elections and what role the opposition will play in shaping the country’s future.
Article Summary: María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday after nearly a year in exile. Her team confirmed her return, in a move likely to increase pressure on interim president Delcy Rodríguez. Machado left Venezuela covertly in December 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize.

Article Title: 'Gotta stop killing them to know who we're dealing with': Trump says top Iranian leaders gone

They get nothing. Yes, we get everything," he said, describing US enforcement of a blockade on Iranian ports and shipping as successful.Despite a ceasefire and efforts to secure a lasting peace agreement, tensions remain high, with Washington continuing to weigh diplomatic and military options.

Article Title: 'Had enough': Thousands protest in Prague against Czech government's public media funding overhaul
Article Text:

Why are Czechs protesting?

Thousands of people gathered in Czech Republic capital Prague on Sunday to protest against thec government's plans to overhaul the funding of public television and radio, warning that the changes could undermine media independence and expose broadcasters to political pressure.The demonstration in the historic Old Town Square and surrounding streets followed an overnight vote in the lower house of parliament that advanced legislation to abolish licence fees paid by households and businesses and replace them with direct funding from the state budget.The bill, backed by Prime Minister Andrej Babis's governing coalition, received initial approval in the early hours of Saturday after lawmakers moved it unexpectedly onto the agenda and curtailed debate. The legislation is now at the committee stage and must clear further parliamentary votes, including approval by the upper house, before becoming law.The proposed reform would cut funding for Czech Television and Czech Radio by around 15 per cent, potentially from next year. Critics argue that replacing licence fees with allocations from the state budget would make public broadcasters more vulnerable to political interference.Protesters accused the government of pushing through the changes without adequate public scrutiny. Demonstrators chanted slogans including “We've had enough” and “Resignation”, demanding that the draft be withdrawn and that the government allow a thorough public debate.Meanwhile, Babis has rejected suggestions that the plan threatens media independence, saying it is intended to improve transparency in funding.The proposal has drawn criticism from opposition parties and international media organisations, which have called for greater scrutiny of the legislation. Some opponents have compared the plans with changes introduced in Hungary under former prime minister Viktor Orban, whose government oversaw an expansion of pro-government media, and reforms in Slovakia under Prime Minister Robert Fico.The European Broadcasting Union, Reporters Without Borders, the International Press Institute and the European Federation of Journalists are among the organisations that have raised concerns. The European Broadcasting Union and 15 other groups also called for further debate and warned against measures that could threaten the broadcasters' financial sustainability.Czech President Petr Pavel has called for greater expert scrutiny, saying the country was among the few in central and eastern Europe where public-service and private media systems worked well.On the other hand, Mikulas Minar, a leading organiser from the Million Moments for Democracy group, told the crowd, “You've gone too far, we won't let this country be destroyed.” He also criticised the timing of the parliamentary vote, saying, “It is mafia syndicates or the Soviet Politburo who make decisions at 4:36.”For some protesters, the proposed changes evoked memories of the country's history of state control over broadcasting.Milan Kotal, a 94-year-old demonstrator, said: “In my lifetime there have already been two state takeovers of our television in Prague: once by the Nazis during the war and then by the Communists until 1989.”“Today the government is allowing itself things we cannot accept,” he added.Public media employees have announced plans to go on strike on November 3, while organisers have called a larger rally at Prague's Letna Park on November 15, two days before the anniversary of the 1989 Velvet Revolution that ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia.Public broadcasters remain an important source of news in the country. Czech Television is the country's most-watched broadcaster across major age groups, while public media rank among the most trusted news sources, according to a 2025 Reuters Institute survey.
Article Summary: Protesters accuse government of pushing through the changes without adequate public scrutiny. The proposed reform would cut funding for Czech Television and Czech Radio by around 15 per cent. Critics argue that replacing licence fees with allocations from the state budget would make public broadcasters more vulnerable to political interference.

Article Title: ‘People have won’: Serbia’s Vucic concedes defeat to student-led oppn in major political shift
Article Text:
File photo: Supporters of the electoral list "Student List - Students Win" celebrate after Aleksandar Vucic, Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) prime ministerial candidate, conceded defeat in the parliamentary election

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you believe is the most important issue the new Students' List government should tackle first? Corruption Economic reform Media freedom 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Tens of thousands of people flooded the streets of Serbia’s capital on Sunday night, bringing traffic to a halt and celebrating after long-time leader Aleksandar Vucic conceded defeat in parliamentary elections to a student-backed opposition movement.Trams and vehicles were halted as crowds filled the city’s main boulevards, with smoke hanging in the air and supporters waving flares. The celebrations marked the culmination of a two-year protest movement that had called for Vucic to step down and for an end to what demonstrators described as rampant corruption — allegations the leader has denied.The election marks a major political shift in the Balkan country, where Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) had held power for 14 years. Vucic said his party’s projections showed the Students’ List winning between 135 and 140 seats in the 250-member Parliament, compared with around 105 for the SNS.“The Students’ List has won,” Vucic told supporters at his party’s election-night event. He blamed independent media, unnamed European countries and what he called an “American deep state” for the defeat.“That is the best thing that happened in my life. We will now breathe freely,” Milica, a law student, told Reuters said as supporters celebrated in Belgrade.Vucic had served as either prime minister or president since 2014 and presided over a period of strong economic growth. But his government faced mounting opposition after a railway station canopy collapsed in Novi Sad in November 2024, killing 16 people. The disaster triggered student-led protests over alleged corruption, cronyism and irregularities in renovation work.The Students’ List was shaped by university students, though students themselves did not appear on the electoral list. Instead, it fielded 250 candidates, including lawyers, professors, actors, farmers and other professionals, in an effort to challenge Vucic’s personalised style of rule and build a broader, non-partisan movement.At the movement’s headquarters, candidates and supporters embraced and cheered as the scale of their victory sank in.“The people have won! The people defeated a dictator! The people will lead Serbia!” said Nebojsa Cosic told Reuters, waving a flag in the street.The movement’s campaign focused on rebuilding the economy and restoring democracy, drawing support from voters disillusioned with established political parties. Supporters travelled by bicycle and on foot through the country to reach voters in rural areas that had traditionally backed Vucic.The election was closely watched by the European Union, as Serbia is a candidate for membership. Monitors reported dozens of suspected irregularities, including ballot photographing that suggested pressure on voters and attempted vote-buying. International and local observers had also raised concerns about detentions, extensive government control over the media, and reports of surveillance and cyberattacks targeting activists.The student-backed victory echoed a recent electoral defeat for Vucic ally Viktor Orbán in Hungary and could resonate across Europe, where youth-led protests have challenged governments over political and economic grievances.The movement now faces the challenge of translating its electoral victory into government, while voters and international observers await the next steps in Serbia’s political transition.
Article Summary: Aleksandar Vucic, Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) prime ministerial candidate, conceded defeat in the parliamentary election. The election marks a major political shift in the Balkan country. The Students' List fielded 250 candidates, including lawyers, professors, actors, farmers and other professionals.

Article Title: 2 killed, 2 injured as assailants in Scorpio open fire outside homes in Punjab’s Moga; 15-20 rounds fired, say eyewitnesses
Article Text:
Two individuals have died and two others are hospitalized following gunfire in Angadpura locality





BATHINDA: Two persons died, and two others sustained serious injuries when unidentified persons fired multiple gunshots from a Black Scorpio SUV late Sunday at Angadpura locality of Moga town.The deceased have been identified as cousins Sahil Jindal and Gagan Jindal, while the injured have been rushed to a hospital.Five people were standing outside their homes that, as per police, some people arrived in a Black Scorpio and fired indiscriminately.Prima facie, it is a case of personal enmity and the family has named some suspects. A probe has been started.While police said the number of rounds fired remains unclear, eyewitnesses said the assailants fired at least 15-20 rounds.Moga SSP Sartaj Singh Chahal said, “We have initiated an investigation. Our teams rushed to the spot immediately. Prima facie, five people were sitting outside their homes when a black Scorpio arrived, and assailants inside opened fire. We have recovered three shells from the spot. A forensic team was also called to the spot. We are checking nearby CCTV cameras.”
Article Summary: Unidentified persons fired multiple gunshots from a Black Scorpio SUV late Sunday at Angadpura locality of Moga town. The deceased have been identified as cousins Sahil Jindal and Gagan Jindal, while the injured have been rushed to a hospital. Police say it is a case of personal enmity and the family has named some suspects.

Article Title: Man killed as Mercedes driven by judge’s minor son hits scooter in Keralam
Article Text:
The deceased was identified as Jayabalakrishnan, son of Rangaswamy Chettiyar of South Chittoor.

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the priority in addressing juvenile driving issues? Strict enforcement of driving laws Greater parental responsibility Stronger penalties for violations 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





KOCHI: A Mercedes-Benz driven by a 17-year-old son of an additional sessions judge rammed into a scooter on Container Road near Maraparamb in Cheranelloor here around 2.20am on Sunday, killing a 55-year-old man.The deceased was identified as Jayabalakrishnan, son of Rangaswamy Chettiyar of South Chittoor.He ran a roadside eatery and was reportedly heading home after closing the shop when the accident occurred. Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery, and a preliminary police investigation indicated that the car hit the scooter from behind.An FIR has been registered under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for rash driving and causing death by negligence. Police later said Section 105, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, would be added following allegations that no strong action was being taken in the case.The 17-year-old was released from the police station earlier as the offences initially invoked were bailable. Police sources said a decision on further action, including apprehending him and producing him before the Juvenile Justice Board, would be taken soon.A senior officer with Cheranelloor police said the minor underwent a medical examination, and the preliminary report indicated that he had not consumed alcohol. A detailed report is awaited. A preliminary investigation indicated that the boy was alone in the car, the officer said.Meanwhile, Jayalakshmi, a relative of the victim, described the accident scene as horrifying. “One of his footwear items was on the road, while the other chappal and helmet were some distance away on the service road. The damage to the vehicles itself showed the intensity of the collision,” she told reporters.She alleged that the minor’s father told her not to question him when she asked why a minor had been allowed to drive. She said she insisted on meeting the boy’s parents after police personnel told her that his father was a judicial officer.Police have not revealed the minor’s details since Section 74 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act prohibits the disclosure of the identity or any other particulars that may lead to the identification of a child in conflict with the law.Police said the teen claimed that the scooter suddenly swerved to avoid waterlogging and he couldn’t stop on time to avoid the collision. There was heavy rain during the early hours on Sunday.The accident comes close on the heels of another high-profile accident here on Oct 11, when a Mini Cooper car driven by a 19-year-old mowed down a scooter, killing three youths. Suhail (19), who was behind the wheel, was inebriated and the car was driven at an extreme speed. He is still in remand. Police later found that the accused had consumed liquor from three different bar hotels before the accident.Meanwhile, Youth Congress leader Shajahan P Y lodged a complaint with home minister Ramesh Chennithala, seeking strong action under Section 119A of the Motor Vehicles Act. The provision holds the guardian of a juvenile or the owner of the vehicle guilty of the contravention in such situations and liable to be proceeded against.However, the guardian or owner will not be liable to punishment if they prove that the offence was committed without their knowledge or that they exercised due diligence to prevent it. The Act also presumes that the juvenile used the vehicle with the consent of the guardian or its owner.
Article Summary: A Mercedes-Benz driven by a 17-year-old son of an additional sessions judge rammed into a scooter on Container Road near Maraparamb in Cheranelloor here around 2.20am. The deceased was identified as Jayabalakrishnan, son of Rangaswamy Chettiyar of South Chittoor.

Article Title: Land, money dispute, broken marriage alliance behind Bengaluru battery IED blast; 3 held
Article Text:
Police arrested three childhood friends, suspected of conspiring to kill one of the injured workers over personal grievances.





BENGALURU:A parcel containing an improvised explosive device (IED) concealed inside a torch battery turned into a deadly trap for two workers at an under-construction building on Jeremaiah Road in Frazer Town.Police suspect the blast was part of a premeditated murder plot stemming from a land dispute, financial disagreements and a broken marriage alliance.East Division police have arrested three persons, Bhurhan Ahmad Burbhuiyya, 20, who works as a welder and electrician in Maski, Raichur district; Jahidull Hussain Burbhuiyya, 27, a salesman at a bakery in Jayanagar; and Sajidull Lashkar, 22, who works in the kitchen of a restaurant in Malleswaram.All three are natives of Dinanathpur in Hailakandi district of Assam.Two persons were injured in the incident: Allauddin, from Dinanathpur and a relative of Jahidull, and Sajidull, a childhood friend of Bhurhan and Jahidull.Both worked at the under-construction building, with duties including painting and security. Allauddin and Jahidull had financial, property and personal issues involving their families.The explosion occurred on October 20 at a building under construction within the jurisdiction of Pulakeshinagar police station.Two workers, Suraj and Allauddin, sustained serious injuries in the blast. Allauddin was later discharged from hospital after receiving treatment.According to police, a painter lodged a complaint after a loud explosion rocked the building’s fifth floor while workers were on duty.A preliminary inspection revealed that an improvised explosive device (IED), concealed inside a torch battery, had detonated, injuring the two workers.Taking the case seriously, deputy commissioner of police (East) Vikram Amathe formed 10 special teams to investigate the incident from multiple angles.Investigators analysed footage from more than 1,500 CCTV cameras and questioned over 100 people as part of the probe. Their efforts led to the arrest of two suspects in Bengaluru. A third accused was subsequently apprehended in Maski and brought in for questioning.During interrogation, police learnt that the three accused were childhood friends of Allauddin who conspired to commit the crime and shared information through a WhatsApp group.The injured worker and all three accused are neighbours.Police said the prime accused, Jahidull, is a cousin of the injured Allauddin.The two had a strained relationship over a land dispute and financial differences in their native village. An issue involving the cancellation of Jahidull’s sister’s marriage is also suspected to have added to the animosity.According to investigators, Jahidull plotted to kill Allauddin and enlisted the help of the other two accused. The trio gathered information through online web applications, purchased raw materials locally and assembled the IED themselves after searching for information about it online.As part of the plan, they concealed the device inside a torch battery, packed it in a parcel and left it at a petty shop near the building, ensuring that the intended target would collect it. Accused Bhurhan then pressured Allauddin on the phone to open the parcel.However, the plan resulted in coworker Suraj opening the parcel.The accused spoke in Hindi, and Allauddin claimed that he did not understand Hindi, triggering the explosion. Suraj, who opened it, suffered serious injuries and is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital.Police said the three accused were produced before a court and taken into police custody for detailed interrogation. The three arrested men have no criminal background.Questioning is continuing to ascertain where they procured the explosives, and further investigation is under way to establish all the circumstances surrounding the conspiracy and the blast and determine whether the UAPA needs to be invoked in the case.
Article Summary: Police suspect the blast was part of a premeditated murder plot stemming from a land dispute, financial disagreements and a broken marriage alliance. East Division police have arrested three persons, Bhurhan Ahmad Burbhuiyya, 20, who works as a welder and electrician in Maski, Raichur district. Jahidull Hussain Burbhusuyya, 27, a salesman at a bakery in Jayanagar; and Sajidull Lashkar, 22, works in the kitchen of a restaurant in Malleswaram. The three arrested men have no criminal background.

Article Title: Class 11 student abducted, raped and murdered in West Bengal's Gaighata, 1 held
Article Text:
A 17-year-old girl was reported abducted, raped, and murdered near the Indo-Bangladesh border in West Bengal (Representative image used for representational purposes)





KOLKATA: A 17-year-old girl, a student of Class 11, was allegedly abducted, raped and murdered near the Indo-Bangladesh border at Gaighata, North 24 Parganas, on Saturday night.Her naked body was recovered from behind a neighbour’s house on Sunday morning, triggering protests in the area.Police arrested Prahlad Das, 23, a resident of Shimulpur in Gaighata and said to have been known to the victim.A Bongaon court remanded him in 10 days of police custody on Sunday afternoon.According to police, the girl had attended a soiree near her house on Saturday night. Her family alleged she received a phone call around 11.30pm and left the event.When she did not return, family relatives, and neighbours searched for her through the night. Her body, bearing multiple injuries, was recovered in the morning.Her aunt said she had last seen the girl on Saturday evening. “She told us she was going to the jalsa with a friend. In the morning, we heard about this horrific incident,” she said.Bongaon Police District SP Bidisha Kalita Dasgupta said a rape and murder case had been registered based on the family’s complaint.A special investigation team headed by the ASP of Bongaon has been formed. A medical board has been constituted for the post-mortem, which will be videographed. A forensic team has been called to collect evidence from the crime scene.“We are investigating whether more people were involved. The accused will be interrogated further,” the SP said.Preliminary questioning has indicated the accused allegedly harboured resentment against the girl over remarks she had made about his mother. Investigators are examining the motive and whether others were involved.A large police contingent including RAF and Combat Force personnel was deployed to bring the situation under control following protests by local residents.Gaighata MLA Subrata Thakur condemned the incident and said his party stood by the victim’s family, demanding the harshest possible punishment.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old girl was reported abducted, raped, and murdered near the Indo- Bangladesh border in West Bengal. Her naked body was recovered from behind a neighbour’s house on Sunday morning, triggering protests in the area. Police arrested Prahlad Das, 23, a resident of Shimulpur in Gaighata and said to have been known to the victim.

Article Title: Delhi Police register case over Jamia Campus trespassing, defacement
Article Text:
Hundreds of students and alumni have gathered at Jamia Millia Islamia for the 14th day of protests.





NEW DELHI: Hundreds of students and alumni gathered at Jamia Millia Islamia Sunday as the agitation demanding the restoration of students’ union elections entered its 14th day. The demonstration continued despite the university’s decision Saturday to shift classes online and close campus gates and libraries until further notice.With police personnel deployed in large numbers and barricades erected outside the university, students reportedly made their way through different entrances to reach the protest site near Gate No. 7. Demonstrators raised slogans, displayed placards and demanded that the gates be reopened to allow others to join the protest. According to some students, the university vice-chancellor, along with some other university members, visited the protest site around noon but left without engaging with the demonstrators. Delhi Police , meanwhile, registered a case on a complaint from the university administration after several individuals allegedly entered the campus without authorisation on Friday. Two MPs and other individuals not associated with Jamia allegedly entered the campus, triggering chaos and tension on the university premises.Police intervened and some of those involved were detained. No one was named as a suspect in the FIR. One person was detained Sunday in connection with the alleged trespassing.Police also added a section related to defacement after “objectionable” slogans and graffiti appeared on the university walls, sources confirmed. The graffiti included messages, such as “Free Kashmir” and “Free Sharjeel Imam”, along with slogans targeting the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. Protesters have denied responsibility for the graffiti.Police are scanning CCTV footage from the university campus and surrounding areas to identify those allegedly involved in the defacement. Investigators are examining the footage and other evidence to establish the sequence of events and ascertain who was responsible. The investigation into the alleged trespassing and defacement is ongoing.Security remained heightened outside the university campus as a precautionary measure to prevent any untoward incident and maintain law and order amid the prevailing tension.The agitation began on Oct 12, with students sitting on a protest and hunger strike demanding the restoration of the university’s students’ union and elections.
Article Summary: Hundreds of students and alumni gathered at Jamia Millia Islamia for the 14th day of protests. Demonstration continued despite the university’s decision to shift classes online and close campus gates and libraries until further notice. Delhi Police registered a case on a complaint from the university administration after several individuals allegedly entered the campus without authorisation on Friday.

Article Title: Delhi building collapse: Father and 33-year-old son killed as old structure caves in at Harsh Vihar
Article Text:
Three bodies were found after a slab of an under-construction house collapsed in Harsh Vihar





NEW DELHI: A 60-year-old man and his 33-year-old son died after a building collapsed in the Harsh Vihar area of Northeast Delhi on Sunday.The deceased have been identified as Chanderpal, 60, and his son, Vijay Kumar, 33. Both were residents of Street number 14 in Harsh Vihar.According to police, information about the collapse at A-4, Milan Garden, was received at the Harsh Vihar police station around 6.46pm on Sunday. A police team subsequently reached the spot.A preliminary inspection revealed that the ground-floor structure of an old building, reportedly being used as a godown, had collapsed along with the first-floor structure above it. The property is reportedly owned by Manoj Kumar.Two fire brigade vehicles, two ambulances and a crane were deployed at the site to assist in the rescue operation. Civil Defence volunteers and a team from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) also joined the efforts.During the overnight rescue operation, the father-son duo was pulled out from beneath the debris and rushed to Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital, where doctors declared them brought dead.The rescue operation was still underway, while police initiated legal proceedings under the relevant provisions of law.Further investigation is in progress to ascertain the circumstances that led to the building collapse.
Article Summary: The deceased have been identified as Chanderpal, 60, and his son, Vijay Kumar, 33. Information about the collapse at A-4, Milan Garden, was received at the Harsh Vihar police station. The ground-floor structure of an old building, reportedly being used as a godown, had collapsed.

Article Title: Crocodile meat bite in Thailand lands Ujjain official in hot water; video emerges

The clip carries the caption, "Trying crocodile for the first time in Thailand," and also contains visuals of dead crocodiles.

INDORE: A taste of the exotic has turned into an unexpected official headache for a Madhya Pradesh civic officer. After a video purportedly showing Ujjain Municipal Corporation building officer Rajkumar Rathore and his wife sampling crocodile meat during a Thailand holiday went viral, the civic body has aksed his if he obtained the mandatory permisiion to travel abroad.Rathore, who is posted as the building officer for Zones 1, 2 and 3 of the Ujjain Municipal Corporation, had taken leave from Oct 19 to 23, municipal commissioner Abhilash Mishra said.However, according to Mishra, Rathore's leave application did not mention that he intended to travel abroad.The controversy erupted after the video, reportedly shared on the social media account of Rathore's wife, showed him and his wife standing near what appears to be a restaurant or food stall, with what is described in the caption as crocodile meat being served to them.The clip carries the caption, "Trying crocodile for the first time in Thailand," and also contains visuals of dead crocodiles.While the crocodile may have been the star of the holiday, it is the officer's foreign travel without the required official permission that has caught the civic body's attention.
