Article Title: After two decades, Jamia Millia Islamia orders student union polls within 15 days of constitution approval; students reject move, vow to continue stir
Article Text:
Jamia Millia Islamia has ordered the holding of students' union elections within 15 days after constitutional approval.

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top priority in resolving the Jamia student protest? Announcing a clear election date Restoring the students’ union Withdrawing disciplinary action Addressing students’ concerns through dialogue 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Jamia Millia Islamia has ordered the resumption of students’ union elections, stating that polls will be held within 15 days of approval of the union’s constitution.The university has also revoked suspension orders and show-cause notices issued to students during the ongoing protest and announced an inquiry into the conduct of security personnel during the agitation.However, protesting students have rejected the administration’s order, calling it ambiguous and insisting that the agitation will continue until their demands are addressed through clear, written commitments.An order issued by Registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi on Monday, October 26, states that elections to the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union (JMISU) will be held 15 days after the union’s constitution is approved. It also provides for a committee to inquire into the actions of security staff during the protest.The order came after the administration held talks with students who had submitted a list of demands, including the restoration of the elected students’ union, withdrawal of disciplinary action and an inquiry into alleged excesses by security personnel.According to the order, the protesting students have agreed to issue a public apology through a press conference for allegedly defamatory statements, actions or social media posts targeting the university administration during the agitation.The posts are to be taken down from social media platforms with immediate effect.The order states that the protest will be called off immediately following its issuance.However, the Jammu & Kashmir Students Association said the order did not provide a definite timeline for approval of the union’s constitution or address the students’ demand for the resignation of the proctor.“Assurances without concrete decisions and a clear roadmap cannot be treated as fulfilment of our demands,” the student organisation said in a statement, adding that the agitation would continue until the administration provided written commitments addressing their concerns.According to the association, Registrar Rizvi arrived on campus around 4.30am on Monday for talks with the protesters. He shared the administration’s order and urged the students to end their agitation, saying their demands had been met.The protest has centred on the demand for the restoration of JMISU, whose elections have not been held since 2006. Four students had been on an indefinite hunger strike, while other protesters sought a time-bound election schedule, withdrawal of disciplinary action and an inquiry into the conduct of security personnel.Amid escalating tensions, the university had earlier shifted classes across courses to online mode and advised students against visiting the campus. It had also announced that gates and libraries would remain closed until further notice.The administration had said a seven-member committee of professors held multiple rounds of talks with the protesters. A committee to draft the JMISU constitution was notified on October 21.Students, however, had argued that setting up the drafting committee was insufficient without a definite election timeline and student representation in the process.The latest order addresses some of their demands, including the withdrawal of disciplinary action and an inquiry into the conduct of security personnel. However, the lack of a fixed deadline for approval of the constitution remains a key point of contention.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Jamia Millia Islamia has ordered the resumption of students’ union elections. The university has also revoked suspension orders and show-cause notices issued to students during the ongoing protest. However, protesting students have rejected the administration’s order, calling it ambiguous.

Article Title: Kochi Mercedes hit-and-run: Judge’s minor son drives car at high speed, kills man; released on bail, now taken into custody again after protests
Article Text:
A minor driving a Mercedes-Benz collided with a scooter, resulting in the death of a 55-year-old man (L).

A minor behind the wheel of a Mercedes-Benz rammed into a scooter





KOCHI: Police took the 17-year-old son of an additional sessions judge into custody again after protests by the family of a man killed when Mercedes-Benz allegedly driven by the minor rammed into his scooter in Cheranelloor, Kochi, in the early hours of Sunday.Police had initially registered a case of causing death by negligence and released the boy on bail from the police station.However, following protests by the victim’s family and a preliminary investigation indicating that the car was being driven at high speed, police invoked Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder.The deceased, Jayabalakrishnan, 55, a resident of South Chittoor, ran a roadside eatery. He was returning home on his scooter after closing his shop when the accident occurred around 2.20am on Container Road near Marapparambu in Cheranelloor.Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery, and a preliminary investigation indicated that the Mercedes hit the scooter from behind. The car is registered in the judge’s name.The initial release of the minor triggered protests outside Cheranelloor police station, where Jayabalakrishnan’s son and daughter, accompanied by activists, demanded that the accused be taken into custody and produced before the Juvenile Justice Board.As the agitation intensified and more people gathered in support of the family, senior police officers intervened. Police subsequently reached the judge’s residence, took the boy into custody and produced him before the board late at night.During the protest, Jayabalakrishnan’s daughter fainted and was taken to hospital, police said.The victim’s family also demanded that a case be registered against the judge for allegedly allowing his minor son to drive the car. Police said they had sought legal opinion on whether the judge could be arraigned in the case and would take a decision on Monday.An earlier police statement said the minor had undergone a medical examination, with preliminary findings indicating that he had not consumed alcohol. A detailed report was awaited.Police sources said the boy had claimed that the scooter suddenly swerved to avoid waterlogging and that he could not stop the car in time to prevent the collision. Heavy rain had lashed the area during the early hours of Sunday.Jayalakshmi, a relative of the victim, described the accident scene as horrifying, pointing to the damage to the vehicles and the distance at which the victim’s footwear and helmet were found.She also alleged that the judge had spoken disrespectfully to the family when they questioned why his minor son had been allowed to drive. The family said it would pursue the case.The incident comes less than three weeks after another fatal crash in Kochi on October 11, when a Mini Cooper allegedly driven at high speed by a 19-year-old who had consumed alcohol hit a scooter, killing three youths. The accused remains in judicial custody.Meanwhile, Youth Congress leader Shajahan P Y had approached state home minister Ramesh Chennithala, seeking action under Section 199A of the Motor Vehicles Act, which provides for action against the guardian or vehicle owner when a juvenile commits a traffic offence using a vehicle.The law provides for exceptions if the guardian or owner can establish that the offence occurred without their knowledge or that they exercised due diligence to prevent it.
Article Summary: Police took the 17-year-old son of an additional sessions judge into custody again after protests by the family of a man killed when Mercedes-Benz allegedly driven by the minor rammed into his scooter. Police had initially registered a case of causing death by negligence and released the boy on bail from the police station.

Article Title: 4 killed, several injured as speeding car hits 'Teshu-Jhanjhi' immersion procession in Firozabad
Article Text:
Firozabad DM Santosh Kumar Sharma said the car was seized and the driver and other occupants were taken into custody.

(With agency inputs)





FIROZABAD: Four people, including women and children, were killed and several others injured after a speeding car rammed into a group of villagers on their way to immerse Tesu-Jhenjhi idols in Uttar Pradesh 's Firozabad district.Firozabad district magistrate Santosh Kumar Sharma stated that the vehicle involved has been seized, and the driver, along with the other occupants, has been taken into custody."A road accident has occurred involving a car, resulting in four deaths and eight injuries. The victims were walking along the roadside in a group that included many women and children from a village when the accident took place. Arrangements are being made to ensure proper medical treatment for those injured. The vehicle involved has been seized, and the driver, along with the other occupants, has been taken into custody, " Santosh Kumar told news agency ANI."A thorough investigation into the causes of the incident will be conducted. Furthermore, we are reaching out to the Chief Minister's Office to request financial assistance for the families of the deceased. Regarding the cause, while it is a matter for investigation, preliminary reports suggest that the driver may have been under the influence of alcohol; the full picture will emerge once the investigation is complete.Most importantly, this is a deeply tragic incident, " Santosh Kumar added.The district administration is arranging specialised medical treatment for the injured and has approached the Chief Minister’s Office to seek financial assistance for the families of the deceased."The entire administration and the government stand with the bereaved families, and we are committed to providing all possible support, including medical care for the injured and other necessary follow-up actions," district magistrate Santosh Kumar Sharma said.Tesu-Jhenjhi is a traditional folk festival celebrated in parts of Uttar Pradesh like Agra, Mathura, Kanpur, Etawah, Orai, and Jhansi.
Article Summary: A speeding car rammed into a group of villagers on their way to immerse Tesu- Jhenjhi idols in Uttar Pradesh's Firozabad district. The victims were walking along the roadside in a group that included many women and children from a village when the accident took place.

Article Title: Pune police write to Google & Apple to take down Rapido from their app stores
Article Text:
Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar confirmed that the police had sent a communication to tech firms

Pune:

TOI





City police, in their efforts to remove bike taxi option from Rapido’s app, reached out to Google and Apple.The move follows last week’s letter from Pune Collector and Regional Transport Authority chairperson Jitendra Dudi, asking police to shut down the bike taxi service.Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar confirmed that the police have written to Google and Apple. “We have already sent communications to Google Play Store and Apple’s App Store to put down Rapido’s application,” he toldPune RTO officials said the service could soon become unavailable unless Rapido secures the necessary approvals. The company’s application seeking approval to operate bike taxis has been pending with the transport department. “They were warned of legal action if they failed to comply with the norms. An FIR was lodged against them last week, and now the RTA chairperson and police have also stepped in,” an RTO official said, requesting anonymity.“If they comply with all requirements under the bike taxi policy, they may get approval. However, their unauthorised operations could complicate matters,” the official said.The bike taxi option remains active on the Rapido app and rides continue across the city despite an FIR being registered against it more than a week ago.Some commuters have questioned the authorities’ push to shut down the service, arguing that public transport remains inadequate and that passengers continue to face overcharging and misbehaviour by some autorickshaw and cab drivers.“I don’t understand why the authorities are so keen to close the service. They cannot ensure adequate public transport and do little when cabbies and autorickshaw drivers overcharge or misbehave. I used the [Rapido bike taxi] service a couple of days ago and found it perfectly fine,” said a Vimannagar resident on the condition of anonymity.Inder Rastogi, a young working professional and friend of the Vimannagar resident, said authorities should focus on regulating the service and improving safety rather than shutting it down. “One of the friends lives in Hinjewadi Phase III and has been watching empty Metro trains run for over a month. The govt has been waiting for the PM to inaugurate the service, with no clarity on when it would begin. Authorities could make bike taxis safer instead of trying to shut them down. The service operates successfully in several cities. They are buckling under pressure from autorickshaw unions,” he said.Autorickshaw unions, meanwhile, criticised the authorities for issuing letters without ensuring that operations cease. They also raised concerns about the verification of riders and passenger safety. “Only a few days ago, the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad caught a bike taxi operator who allegedly had links with a terrorist organisation in Pakistan. It is high time the service was stopped,” said Keshav Kshirsagar, president of Maharashtra Kamgar Sabha and Indian Gig Workers Front.
Article Summary: Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar confirmed that the police have written to Google and Apple. The bike taxi option remains active on the Rapido app and rides continue across the city despite an FIR being registered against it more than a week ago.

Article Title: Omar Abdullah to MLAs: Stop sending WhatsApp messages, knocking on my and Farooq’s doors for ministerial berths; opposition calls it ‘cult of self’
Article Text:
J&K chief minister ​Omar Abdullah





SRINAGAR: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah , after meeting Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha on Saturday, said a cabinet expansion was on the cards and urged party colleagues to stop sending him lengthy WhatsApp messages and book-length profiles seeking ministerial berths.He also advised them against knocking on his door or that of his father and National Conference president, Dr Farooq Abdullah, to lobby for ministerial positions. The opposition described Omar’s portrayal of his party MLAs as demeaning to the political class and called it “the cult of self”.“The lieutenant governor sahab returned to Srinagar. In the meantime, his health had not been good, so I wanted to inquire about his well-being. There are also several issues on which it was necessary to meet him and seek his opinion from time to time. It had been a long time since I met him, so I sought an appointment today. He gave me time,” Omar told reporters after meeting the LG.“I know you people are not interested in anything else. You want to know whether I discussed the cabinet reshuffle with the LG sahab. Yes, absolutely. I sought an appointment with him for the expansion (of cabinet) and requested him to fix a time in the first two or three days of next week.So that I will make some changes and expand my council of ministers,” Omar said.He said the LG would fix a time for the process.“Now that I have told you about the reshuffle, I want to make a request to my colleagues, as news might have already spread about next week’s reshuffle. There is no need to knock on Farooq Abdullah’s door, my door or anyone else’s door,” Omar said.“The decision about who will become a minister has been taken. I request my colleagues to be patient. What is destined for them will happen. First, it is in God’s hands and then we took the decision. Whoever is destined to become a minister will become one. But please, do not knock on doors now. Do not send me WhatsApp messages,” he said.“I am receiving so many WhatsApp messages, with people writing lengthy resumes and sending me entire books. It is as if I do not know these people. They are sending me their complete biodata, as though I am not already familiar with them,” he said.“So please, do not send WhatsApp messages, call or knock on doors. Whatever has to happen will happen in the next two or three days,” Omar said.Omar was sworn in on Oct 16, 2024, along with five ministers, including deputy CM Surinder Choudhary. At present, three cabinet berths remain vacant. Under the norms, the strength of the council of ministers cannot exceed 10% of the total strength of the assembly. The J&K assembly has 90 members, capping the council of ministers at nine.Omar has allocated deputy CM Surinder Kumar Choudhary the portfolios of public works, industries and commerce, mining, labour and skill development. Sakeena Itoo handles health and medical education, school education, higher education and social welfare. Javed Ahmed Rana oversees water resources, forests, environment and tribal affairs. Javid Ahmad Dar is tasked with agriculture, panchayati raj and cooperatives. Satish Sharma is responsible for food, consumer affairs, transport, science and IT, youth affairs, sports and training.Leader of Opposition and BJP's Sunil Sharma, who has been claiming that the NC will "implode" if Omar goes ahead with the cabinet expansion, said, “The CM is behaving like a king. Like a king, he doesn’t like people visiting his home. He wants only a close coterie around him, with everyone else reduced to reporting to them. He is out to demean his own MLAs and has repeatedly humiliated them inside and outside the Assembly,” he added.Peoples Conference chairman Sajad Lone sharply reacted to Omar’s statement, calling it “the cult of self”.“I watched CM sahib talking to the media after meeting LG sahib. What a contemptuous and disdainful way of asking his party MLAs to not pester him for a ministerial berth. I honestly can’t believe that these MLAs are comfortable with such belittling and humiliating remarks,” Lone said.“If you are unable to accommodate them in the cabinet, you can spare them from public humiliation,” he added.“Anyway, these are internal party matters and I should not have commented. But there is always a spillover. You may direct the derision at your own members, but it invariably belittles the political class. I wonder how these elected members face their electors when they know they are treated like unworthy and incapable schoolboys,” Lone added.
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah said a cabinet expansion was on the cards. He urged party colleagues to stop sending him lengthy WhatsApp messages and book-length profiles seeking ministerial berths. Opposition described Omar’s portrayal of his party MLAs as demeaning to the political class and called it “the cult of self”

Article Title: Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati, one of India's fastest U-23 sprinters in 2025, and 400m runner Malay Barik killed in late-night road accident on Cuttack highway
Article Text:
Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati and Malay Barik, two talented athletes from Odisha, tragically lost their lives in an accident





BHUBANESWAR: Two promising Odisha athletes, Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati, one of India's fastest under-23 sprinters in 2025, and 400m runner Malay Barik, were killed in a road accident on the Cuttack highway late Wednesday night.Dondapati had emerged as one of the country's fastest sprinters in the under-23 category in 2025, while Barik competed in the 400m event. Their deaths have left Odisha's sporting fraternity mourning the loss of two young athletes.Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi expressed grief over their deaths in a social media post."Deeply saddened by the tragic demise of athletes Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati and Malaya Barik in a road accident. Their untimely passing is a profound loss to Odisha's sporting fraternity," Majhi said.Offering condolences to the bereaved families, he prayed to Mahaprabhu Shri Jagannath to give them strength to cope with the loss and grant eternal peace to the departed souls.
Article Summary: Mrutyam Jayaram Dondapati, one of India's fastest under-23 sprinters in 2025, and 400m runner Malay Barik, were killed in a road accident on the Cuttack highway late Wednesday night. Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi expressed grief over their deaths.

Article Title: Tiger Shroff firing: Accused practised shooting near Mumbai before attack, bullet hit bed during accidental discharge in Andheri hotel room
Article Text:
The three accused in the Tiger Sroff firing case

Poll Vote & Share your view What are the most effective measures to prevent firing incidents targeting public figures? Stronger surveillance and intelligence gathering Stricter action against illegal weapon supply networks 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





MUMBAI: Investigations into the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff have revealed that the accused allegedly practised shooting at a location near Mumbai before carrying out the attack.Crime Branch officials said the accused identified the location where they had tested the firearm during interrogation. One of them allegedly fired two rounds, while another fired one round to check whether the weapon was functioning properly.Police have also learnt that the firearm accidentally went off while being tested inside a hotel room in Andheri, with the bullet hitting the bed.Based on information gathered during interrogation, police are examining the alleged firing practice site near Mumbai and investigating the preparations made before the incident.Meanwhile, Mumbai Police arrested two more suspects in connection with the firing case on Wednesday, taking the total number of arrests to 10. The two accused are expected to be produced before a court in Sonipat, Haryana, to seek transit remand. Once the court grants approval, they will be brought to Mumbai for further questioning.According to reports, the two suspects allegedly played a significant role in supplying weapons linked to the case.Investigators are probing their links with the other accused and their alleged involvement in planning and executing the incident.In another development, investigators will examine an audio clip containing a threat allegedly directed at Tiger Shroff. Officials plan to compare the voice in the recording with voice samples maintained in databases by the Punjab and Delhi Police.These databases reportedly contain recordings of individuals allegedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. Police units in Punjab, Delhi and Rajasthan maintain separate collections of voice samples that can help verify the identities of suspected speakers.Similar verification procedures have previously been undertaken in investigations involving audio clips linked to threats allegedly received by actor Salman Khan, actor Aamir Khan, filmmaker Rohit Shetty and the late politician Baba Siddique, among others.Investigators are examining the available audio evidence and other leads to establish the identities of those involved and determine the extent of their alleged roles in the firing case.
Article Summary: The accused allegedly practised shooting at a location near Mumbai before carrying out the attack. One of them allegedly fired two rounds, while another fired one round to check whether the weapon was functioning properly. The firearm accidentally went off while being tested inside a hotel room in Andheri, with the bullet hitting the bed.

Article Title: Over 3 lakh Punjab govt employees continue mass leave on day-3 as talks fail; bus staff extend strike indefinitely
Article Text:
Bus staff protest in Patiala on Wednesday





CHANDIGARH: Over three lakh Punjab govt employees took mass casual leave on Wednesday over pending demands, disrupting work across govt offices. Talks with the state govt failed to break the deadlock, with employees deciding to continue their two-day protest on Thursday. Meanwhile, the Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC Contract Workers’ Union extended its statewide strike indefinitely, affecting bus services.Employee representatives met chief secretary KAP Sinha at 4 pm after the govt released minutes of an earlier meeting with chief minister Bhagwant Mann, as demanded by unions. However, the nearly two-hour meeting remained inconclusive.Sukhchain Singh Khaira, coordinator of the Joint Action Committee leading the agitation, said work across govt offices, including directorates, was affected. Sahil Sharma, general secretary of the Punjab Civil Secretariat Employees Union, alleged the govt was delaying a resolution by asking unions to reiterate demands already raised in previous meetings.A 39-member delegation of employees and pensioners later met officials but said it received no clear assurances on several demands. They said the govt had clarified that temporary teachers described as regularised had only been given “security of tenure”, without the financial benefits available to regular employees.The delegation also said the govt had no roadmap for Anganwadi, ASHA and mid-day meal workers.The future course of the agitation will be decided at a meeting in Ludhiana on Oct 25. Employees are demanding release of pending dearness allowance (DA) instalments and arrears, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), regularisation of contractual staff, revision of pensions, restoration of 37 discontinued allowances and the cashless health scheme. They have also sought withdrawal of notifications imposing central pay scales and a three-year probation period.The standoff continues despite a Sept 18 meeting between Mann and employee and pensioner representatives, when the chief minister announced an 8% DA hike in two instalments of 4% each from Oct 1 and promised regular monthly meetings.Meanwhile, transport workers extended their strike after talks with a cabinet minister failed to resolve demands for regularisation under service rules, direct departmental contracts for outsourced workers and withdrawal of police cases linked to earlier protests.Union general secretary Shamsher Singh said proposals covering around 1,400 outsourced Punjab Roadways employees and more than 1,700 PRTC workers remained pending. A Sept 21 govt letter had set a one-month deadline to shift workers from outsourcing agencies to direct contracts, but it passed without implementation, he said. A proposal to withdraw cases had also been sent to the Punjab DGP, but no further action had followed despite workers securing bail.The union plans a joint demonstration with Theka Mulazam Sangharsh Morcha in Dirba, the constituency of transport and finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema. Workers from all 27 depots and two sub-depots plan to assemble in Mohali and march towards Punjab Vidhan Sabha and the chief minister’s official residence.Union representatives alleged that shortages of spare parts and tyres had grounded several buses and criticised PRTC management for issuing show-cause notices and termination warnings. However, PRTC GM Operations A S Tiwana said more than 800 of the corporation’s 1,250 buses operated on Wednesday. He said management had proposed bringing around 1,719 outsourced employees under contractual terms.Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh called the mass leave a sign of a deepening crisis of confidence between the Mann govt and its employees. He demanded immediate talks and time-bound solutions, accusing the govt of prioritising publicity over public grievances.
Article Summary: Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC Contract Workers’ Union extended its statewide strike indefinitely, affecting bus services. Talks with the state govt failed to break the deadlock, with employees deciding to continue their two-day protest on Thursday.

Article Title: Mettur Dam water release for Cauvery delta irrigation to end tonight after 45 days
Article Text:
The Mettur Dam





SALEM: Water release from Mettur Dam for irrigation in the Cauvery delta will stop on Thursday night, as the 45-day schedule that began on September 1 comes to an end.Chief minister C Joseph Vijay opened the dam for irrigation after reservoir levels improved following inflows from catchment areas in Karnataka. The water level stood at about 91.56 feet against the dam’s full capacity of 120 feet when releases began. The schedule was intended to support irrigation across the Cauvery delta region.On Thursday morning, the reservoir level stood at 59.13 feet, down from about 91.56 feet on September 1. Storage was recorded at 24.04 tmc ft, while inflow had fallen to 696 cusecs.Water Resources Department (WRD) officials said the dam’s storage levels and future inflows would determine any further decisions on irrigation releases.
Article Summary: Water release from Mettur Dam for irrigation in the Cauvery delta will stop on Thursday night. The 45-day schedule that began on September 1 comes to an end. Chief minister C Joseph Vijay opened the dam for irrigation after reservoir levels improved following inflows from Karnataka.

Article Title: 7 years apart, anti-drug activist Parvinder Jhota’s killing revives memories of Neha Shoree murder
Article Text:
Neha Shoree, Parvinder Jhota (File Photos)

Neha Shoree: A licence cancelled and then a killing

Parvinder Singh Jhota: The 2023 dispute that preceded his killing

A continuing challenge for Punjab





CHANDIGARH: Seven years after Punjab drug licensing officer Neha Shoree was shot dead in her office, the killing of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in Mansa has brought renewed attention to the risks faced by those who challenge alleged illegal drug sales in the state.The two cases, separated by more than seven years, involved different circumstances and accused persons. But both brought allegations of illegal drug sales into focus and raised questions about the enforcement of laws governing medicines and addictive substances.Shoree, a zonal licensing drug authority, was shot dead in her office in Kharar near Mohali on March 29, 2019. Jhota, 45, was shot dead in Mansa on October 13, 2026, while confronting a medical store owner over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs.Four other people were injured in the firing, which was captured during Jhota’s Facebook Live broadcast.Shoree was selected as a drug inspector through the Punjab Public Service Commission in 2007 and joined the health department in Ropar that October. In 2013, she was given the responsibility of district zonal licensing authority.On March 29, 2019, she was shot dead at her office by Balwinder Singh, a chemist from Morinda whose shop licence she had cancelled in 2009, police said.During her tenure as a drug inspector in Ropar, Shoree had raided shops and seized banned drugs.Her parents alleged that the drug mafia was behind the killing because she had exposed the sale of intoxicants in the Ropar and Kharar region.“We want to question Prime Minister Narendra Modi that you have been assuring to make a drug-free country but here women officers are being killed by drug mafia,” her mother and paternal aunt said, according to a TOI report published on March 31, 2019.The family’s allegations prompted demands for a wider investigation. The then Punjab chief minister, Capt Amarinder Singh, subsequently handed the probe to ADGP Prabodh Kumar, director of the Bureau of Investigation.However, in December 2019, police informed the Punjab and Haryana high court that their investigation had found no involvement of the drug mafia or any other person besides the accused.Shoree’s family continued to question the findings and seek further investigation.In September 2019, the Punjab government approved financial benefits of around Rs 31 lakh for her family. Shoree’s killing had also prompted scrutiny of the licensing process and the circumstances surrounding the accused’s arms licence.Jhota became known in Mansa for confronting medical store owners whom he accused of selling intoxicating pills, synthetic drugs and other prohibited substances. He recorded confrontations and shared videos on social media.His dispute with medical store owner Ashwani Kumar dated back to July 2023. Jhota had allegedly put a garland of shoes around Kumar’s neck in a public confrontation, accusing him of selling synthetic drugs.A case was registered against Jhota, who was arrested and spent nearly two months in jail. He was released on September 11, 2023, after the complainant approached the court to withdraw the complaint.The case against Kumar concerning the alleged sale of prohibited substances remained pending.Jhota continued his campaign. On the morning of October 13, 2026, he reportedly met an elderly man who had bought synthetic drugs from a medical store and took him to Kumar’s shop to question the owner about the alleged sale.The confrontation escalated as Jhota livestreamed it on Facebook. Kumar allegedly pulled out a firearm and opened fire inside the shop before following the injured activist into the street and firing again. Jhota was hit by three bullets and died at Mansa Civil Hospital. Four others were also injured.In the video, Jhota is heard saying, “maar mainu, maar mainu” (kill me).Kumar fled after the shooting and was arrested in Rajasthan’s Salasar on October 14. Police also detained an alleged associate accused of helping him escape.Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, a retired Army serviceman, refused to cremate his son until those responsible were brought to justice.“I am still alive and pledge to fight against the drug peddlers as my son was waging a war against them. I am also ready to take a bullet if the peddlers are not taken to task,” Bhim Singh said at Mansa Civil Hospital.The killings have brought renewed attention to the state’s efforts to curb drug abuse and the alleged illegal sale of addictive pharmaceutical substances. Following Jhota’s murder, the Punjab government stepped up inspections of chemist shops.The two cases must be viewed in their individual contexts: Shoree was a government officer carrying out licensing duties, while Jhota was an activist who publicly confronted people he accused of selling prohibited substances.Investigators in Shoree’s case said they found no evidence of anyone else being involved in her murder, while the investigation into Jhota’s killing concerns a separate accused and a separate dispute.Their deaths, years apart, have nevertheless renewed questions about the availability of addictive substances, the enforcement of drug-sale regulations and the safety of people who seek to expose alleged violations.
Article Summary: Neha Shoree, a zonal licensing drug authority, was shot dead in her office in Kharar near Mohali on March 29, 2019. Parvinder Singh Jhota, 45, was killed in Mansa on October 13, 2026, while confronting a medical store owner over the alleged sale of synthetic drugs. Both cases, separated by more than seven years, involved different circumstances and accused persons.

Article Title: ‘Don’t trouble me, I’ll commit suicide’: Absconding in Shiva Sharma death case, model Shraddha Dubey releases another video
Article Text:
Shraddha Dubey, accused of killing her businessman boyfriend, Shiva Sharma, has released another.

The 1st video





LUCKNOW: Model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, named as the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old restaurant owner Shiva Sharma in Lucknow, has released another video on Thursday claiming that the two had been dating for the past two months and that Sharma was under a massive debt.In the five-minute-long video, Dubey recounted the events leading up to Sharma’s death.Dubey alleged that Sharma had been receiving calls from people he had borrowed money from and had repeatedly told her that he would die by suicide if he could not repay the loans.She said she could show screenshots to support her claims.In the video, Dubey also appealed to people to stop harassing her, warning that she would die by suicide if the alleged torture continued.“Think why would someone kill someone and throw them from their own apartment,” she said, questioning the allegations against her.She urged the media not to spread rumours without evidence. Referring to Sharma’s mother, Dubey alleged that she had started a quarrel with her driver in the hospital. She then said, “It's not like you have lost a son, I have lost my boyfriend.”Dubey claimed that she and Sharma had not spoken to each other for six to seven days before the incident.On October 7, Sharma allegedly contacted her driver through a tea vendor and was crying, she said."Then I called him twice from my number. He did not pick up the call at that time. Later, he called me around 2am. I asked him what happened to which he asked me to meet him. We met, went to cafe where he ordered coffee for me and juice for himself," she said, adding that he had a "lot of beers" before meeting her."Later, both of us went to my place. While he drove my car, my driver took his car," she said.Dubey said her sister, Rashmi, visited her home on October 8 to discuss a puja for Navratri. She denied her sister's involvement in the case, claiming that Rashmi barely knew Sharma and had hardly spoken to him."My sister has nothing to do with this case. She did not even know Shiva that well. She never spoke to him...My sister and I, we went for a walk that evening. Shiva's friends joined us - one of them was Ashwini Mishra and other named Harsh. We all went for a long drive. I spoke to Shiva, his mother, brother-in-law, and sister too that day," she said.Recounting the day Sharma died, Dubey claimed that he appeared depressed on October 9. She said they woke up and made tea before he went to the washroom."I don't even know what it was. We woke up, made tea. Shiva went to the washroom. Usually, he would never close the main gate. But this time, he did. I asked my sister to go check up on him after a while. As soon as she opened the gate, he jumped from the balcony," she said.Dubey alleged that Sharma's mother accused them of murder and assaulted her driver when she arrived at the hospital."It will be recorded on the hospital's camera. Without knowing anything, she accused us of murder. Without thinking, she blamed us for murder. She blamed us so badly that we might not be able to get out of that blame for life," she said.Earlier, Dubey had released another video denying any wrongdoing and claiming that Sharma’s death was a case of suicide, not murder.She also urged the media to stop linking her to politicians and senior officials, saying she was willing to appear before the police and record her statement.“Just because someone follows me or is connected to me on Instagram does not mean I know them or have any relationship with them,” she had said.Dubey had also denied being absconding and claimed she wanted to cooperate with investigators.“I am not missing. I want to come before the police and tell them everything I know. I want to place the complete truth before them,” she said in the earlier video.Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area. According to police sources, he had been in a relationship with Dubey for around four months.Following his death, Sharma’s mother, Ranjana Sharma, lodged an FIR accusing Dubey, her sister Rashmi, driver Adil and others of murdering her son. The family has alleged that Dubey pushed Sharma from the building, a claim investigators are examining.Lucknow Police have announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each for information leading to the arrest of Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and Tanveer Ali alias Danish in connection with the case.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey claims her boyfriend, Shiva Sharma, was under a massive debt. Dubey says Sharma had been receiving calls from people he had borrowed money from and had repeatedly told her that he would die by suicide if he could not repay the loans. Sharma died on October 9 after falling from the fourth floor of his apartment in Lucknow.
